* * *
 (SCCH3) 3 M.V.C.No.895/2020  JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ for the death of Sri.C.Ravi, in the road traffic accident occurred on 16.10.2019.
02.

The brief facts are as under: It is submitted that on 16.10.2019 at about 02.00 p.m when the deceased namely C.Ravi was standing on a footpath at Gollapalle Village, on ChittoorPiler Road,
Irala Mandal, Chittoor Dist, Andra Pradesh, at that time one Auto rickshaw bearing No.AP03X 4819 was proceeding towards Patoor Village from Damalacheruvu Village, at high speed, in rash and negligent manner, lost control over the vehicle and dashed violently against said C.Ravi.
Due to this said C.Ravi fell down and sustained grievous head injuries.
Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Ramadevi Super Speciality hospital, Tirupathi, but during the course of treatment he succumbed to the injuries.

Then the dead body was shifted to SVRR Government hospital,
Tirupathi, wherein Post mortem was conducted.
The petitioners have spent (SCCH3) 4 M.V.C.No.895/2020 Rs.1,50,000/ towards treatment, transportation, funeral obsequies and other incidental charges.
Due to the death of C.Ravi the petitioners being the wife and parents are put to lot of mental agony and untold misery.
That the deceased prior to the accident was hale and healthy and was working as a Mason and earning Rs.20,000/ p.m.
The accident occurred is solely due to the rash and negligent driving of auto rickshaw driver.
A criminal case was also registered against driver of said auto driver.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending auto rickshaw.
Hence, both respondents are liable to pay the compensation.
Hence this petition.
03. After service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed written statement.
04. The averments of the written statement of respondent No.1 is as under: It is false that the accident took place due to the negligence of the auto rickshaw driver.
But it is due to the fault of deceased only.
It is false that the deceased was earning Rs.20,000/ p.m.

This respondent has Smt.R.Vinayaki vs Sri.M.Sattar Sab on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154380636/
2 denied the relationship of the petitioners with the (SCCH3) 5 M.V.C.No.895/2020 deceased.
The auto driver has valid driving licence and it was duly insured with the respondent No.2.

If the court comes to the conclusion that the petitioners are entitled for the compensation then the respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation and prays to dismiss the petition against this respondent.
05. The averments of the written statement of respondent No.2 is as under: The respondent No.1 has not intimated about the accident.
This respondent has denied issuance of policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Auto rickshaw.
The auto driver did not possessed valid driving licence on the date of accident.
The petitioners are not the legal heirs and dependents on the deceased.
This respondent denies manner of accident, age, occupation and income of the deceased.
The accident took place due to the negligent act of the deceased only who without observing the vehicles standing on the footpath.
The accident is not due to the negligent act of auto driver.
The auto is not involved in this accident.
The claim of the petitioners are highly exorbitant and hence prays to dismiss the petition.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.2 and one eye witness were got examined as PW.1 and 2 and got marked 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to 14 and closed their side.

Even by way of confrontation one document was got marked as Ex.P.15 during the course of crossexamination of RW.1.
07.
By way of rebuttal, the Deputy Manager of respondent No.2 was got examined as RW.1 and got marked one document as Ex.R.1 and closed their side.
08. Heard arguments from both sides.
The petitioners have filed written arguments.
09. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed:  ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioners proves that when the deceased namely C.Ravi was standing on footpath at Gollapalle Village, ChittoorPiler Road, Irala Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, one Auto rickshaw bearing No. AP03 X4819 came from Damalacheruvu Village, in high speed and lost control and dashed against the deceased, due to this he had sustained grievous injuries and succumbed during the course of treatment?
(SCCH3) 7 M.V.C.No.895/2020 02.
Whether petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased C.Ravi?
03. Whether the respondent No.2 proves that auto driver did not hold valid driving licence on the date of accident?
04. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount & from whom?

05. What order or award?

10. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under: Issue No.1 In affirmative Issue No.2 In affirmative Issue No.3 In negative Issue No.4 In partly Affirmative Issue No.5 As per final order for the following:
REASONS 11. Issues No.1 and 2: These issues will be taken at one stretch for my consideration in order to (SCCH3) 8 M.V.C.No.895/2020 avoid repetition of facts as they are inter related with each other.

It is the grievance of the petitioners that the deceased C.Ravi died in road traffic accident which took place on 16.10.2019 due to the rash and negligent manner driving of auto rickshaw driver bearing No.AP03X4819.
Further they have contended that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners have lost their bread earner and facing financial problems and mental stress.
Hence, they have claimed compensation.

12. Per contra, the same was denied by respondents No.1 and 2 and contended that the accident did not took place due to the negligence of auto rickshaw driver but due to negligence of deceased himself.
Hence the petitioners are not entitled for compensation.
13. In order to prove this, the petitioner No.2 was got examined himself as PW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the petition in his affidavit.
The PW.1 in his crossexamination admitted that "The petitioner No.1 is my daughterinlaw.
She is aged about 30 years.
She is doing coolie work.
She is not residing with us.
(SCCH3) 9 M.V.C.No.895/2020 Complaint is given by my daughterinlaw.
It is true that as per the documents produced deceased was aged about 38 years as on the date of accident.
I have not produced any documents to show that deceased was earning Rs.20,000/ per month".
Further the PW.1 had denied all other suggestions of the respondents.
The PW.1 had not seen the accident.
He had deposed based on the available documents on record.

14. Further in support of the case the petitioners have got examined one of the eye witness as PW.2 who had deposed that when he was standing at new bus stop at Gollapalle Village, on Patoor Damalacheruvu Road i.e., ChittoorPiler road, Irala Mandal, Chittoor District, Andra Pradesh, he had seen the accident occurred in between the deceased and the auto rickshaw which came in negligent manner and dashed against the deceased who was standing in front of milk booth.
Due to this the deceased fell down and sustained grievous head injuries.
Then he was shifted to Ramadevi Super Speciality hospital, Tirupathi.
He came to know on next day during course of treatment the injured C.Ravi succumbed to the injuries.
Later the police have recorded his statement.

4 15.
In his cross examination the PW.2 has admitted that "I am residing at Guvvalapalle village.
C.Ravi is my brother.
The accident took place at Gollapalle.
That my brother came to Gollapalle bus stand and I went to see him and at that time the accident took place.
That my brother came to me and was standing there only.
I saw the auto from 25 feet away.
I cannot say the auto number.
The said auto was blue color.
It is true that in the complaint it is stated that I was not present in the accident place, but one Praveen was present".
Eventhough the PW.2 had denied all suggestions of the respondents counsel but it is true that he was not present in the accident place as per the averments of the complaint.
But the PW.2 is cited as eye witness No.6 in the chargesheet.
16. Per contra, the respondent No.2 got examined its Deputy Manager as RW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the written statement in his affidavit.
17. The RW.1 in his cross examination has admitted that "It is false that policy bearing No.P0019300033/4103/103772 was issued to the auto bearing No.AP03X4819.
It is true that we are having branch office at Andrapradesh.
I came to know that the (SCCH3) 11 M.V.C.No.895/2020 fake policy at the time of filing written statement.
We have not taken any action or lodged complaint with respect to fake policy.
We have not enquired about the policy with branch office, Andrapradesh".
18. The RW.1 has got marked the authorization letter as per Ex.R.1.

Apart from Ex.R.1 the respondent No.2 have not produced any documents or not produced any supportive and cogent evidence to believe that they have not issued the policy and the respondent No.1 had created the policy.
19. During the course of cross examination of RW.1 the copy of policy was confronted to him and got marked as Ex.P.15.
Eventhough he had denied the Ex.P.15, but there are no grounds to disbelieve it.

When the respondent No.2 came to know that the policy was fake at the time of filing written statement then what prevented to adduce rebuttal evidence in this regard or produced any documents to show that they have not issued policy.
So in absence of any documents simply taking allegation in the written statement does not serve any purpose.
The attitude of the respondent No.2 shows that they want to escape from the liability and nothing more.
Hence as per (SCCH3) 12 M.V.C.No.895/2020 Ex.P.15 it is true that as on the date of accident the offending auto has valid policy.
20. Further in support of his case, the PW.1 got marked entire police documents as per Ex.P.1 to 9.

On perusal of these documents, it is clear that the concerned I.O after investigation have filed Charge sheet against the driver of offending Auto rickshaw for the alleged offences punishable U/s 304(A) of IPC.
Even as per Ex.P.9 the concerned I.O have stated that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of auto rickshaw only.
21. It is pertinent to note that the PW.1 had marked the Sketch as per Ex.P.4.
It is true that as per Ex.P.4 the accident took place at G.Gollapalle road, Damalu Tank road and Patur side road near Milk Centre at new bus stop.
So as per Ex.P.5 the IMV report no damages found and it does not mean that the accident does not occurred.

5 22.

The counsel for petitioners have relied upon decision reported in a) 2020 ACJ 2131 - United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Satinder Kaur and others - It is observed that when the deceased was working as labour and (SCCH3) 13 M.V.C.No.895/2020 loss of love and affection to be comprehended in loss of consortium.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Satinder Kaur and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 23 . Hence eventhough the respondents have contended that the accident took place due to the negligence of the deceased only and the auto driver did not possessed valid driving licence on the date of accident, but in this support they have not produced any documents.
The oral evidence of the Rw.1 is not to believe the contention of the respondent No.2.
Hence even on perusal of the sketch the alleged negligence of the deceased is not found out.

Hence with the available documents and in absence of supportive documents by the respondents, I am of opinion that the son of petitioner No.2 died due to the accidental injuries only caused by the offending auto rickshaw driver.

24. Further the petitioners in order to prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased have produced Notarized copy of Aadhaar cards of petitioners No.2 and 3, ration card as per Ex.P.10 to 12 and xerox copy of Aadhaar cards of deceased and petitioner No.1.

So, on basis of these documents, I am of opinion that the petitioners No.1 to 3 who are the wife and parents of the deceased can be considered as dependents and legal heirs of (SCCH3) 14 M.V.C.No.895/2020 deceased.

Hence with the available documents I am of opinion that the petitioners have proved that the son of the petitioner No.2 died in the accident caused by the auto rickshaw driver due to his rash and negligent driving.
Hence, I answered issues No.1 and 2 in affirmative.
25. Issue No.3: The respondent No.2 contend that the auto driver did not hold driving licence on the date of accident.
In this regard the respondent No.2 have not adduced any supportive evidence.
Hence under these circumstances it is just and proper to look into the available documents i.e police records.

The concerned I.O after completion of investigation has filed chargesheet against the auto driver, but they have not stated anything as to not holding driving licence by the said offending auto driver.
Hence I answered the issue No.3 in negative.
26. Issue No.4:

As per above findings, it is clear that the accident took place due to negligent driving of the offending auto rickshaw driver and the son of the petitioner No.2 died during the course of treatment due to fatal injuries.

Hence the petitioners (SCCH3) 15 M.V.C.No.895/2020 No.1 to 3 being the dependents of deceased are entitled for compensation as under:
a) Loss of dependency:- The petitioners submitted that the deceased was aged about 35 years as on the date of accident.
To prove the same, they have produced xerox copy of Aadhaar card of deceased which reveals that the deceased was born in the year 1981.
According to it the age of the deceased as on the date of accident would be 39 years and the same is considered for calculating the compensation.
So, as per Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 the multiplier applicable is "15" and the same is considered.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners have stated that the deceased was doing Mason work and earning Rs.20,000/ per month.

In order to prove the income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any Smt.R.Vinayaki vs Sri.M.Sattar Sab on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154380636/
6 documents.
Under these circumstances it is just and proper to consider the notional income.

The accident took place in the year 2019 and the notional income for the said year comes to Rs.14,000/
.
Hence I just feel it proper to fix the notional income at Rs.14,000/ per month.

(SCCH3) 16 M.V.C.No.895/2020 Since the deceased has left three dependents, as per Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 if the dependents are 2 to 3, then personal deduction is to be 1/3rd.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, in this case 1/3 rd deduction has to be done towards personal expenses.
So, after deduction of 1/3rd (Rs.4,666/), then the income comes to Rs.9,334/.
As above stated that apart from the deceased there are no one to look after the petitioners.
As per Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 the petitioners are entitled for future prospects.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deceased being self employed and aged below 40 years, then 40% (Rs.3,733/) to be added towards future prospects, the income for calculation comes to Rs.13,067/.
Hence the petitioners are entitled for Rs.13,067 x 12 x 15 = Rs.23,52,060/ under this head.
b) Loss of estate and funeral expenses:

Since it is settled law in National Insurance Company Ltd.,
Vs Pranay Sethi and others case in (SCCH3) 17 M.V.C.No.895/2020 AIR 2017 SC 5157
that the dependents would be entitled for loss of estate to the extent of Rs.15,000/ and funeral expenses to the extent of Rs.15,000/, as such I award the same.
c) Loss of consortium:

In this case the petitioner No.1 being the widow of the deceased is entitled for Rs.40,000/ towards spousal consortium and petitioners No.2 and 3 being the parents of the deceased are entitled for Rs.40,000/ each towards filial consortium as per Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors case and Magma General Insurance Company case in (2018) 18 SCC 130.
Hence I award the same.
d). Towards medical expenses:
The PW.1 has got marked entire medical bills as per Ex.P.13 which amounts to Rs.40,250/.
On perusal of Medical bills, it is noticed that Sl.No.2 to 5 are the bills for Rs.2,160/, Rs.2,200/, Rs.246/ and Rs.1,200/ and they are included in Sl.No.1, hence the said amount has to be deducted.
There is no serious dispute with regard to other medical bills produced and marked by the PW.1.
(SCCH3) 18 M.V.C.No.895/2020 Hence after deducting Rs.5,806/, the petitioners are entitled for Rs.34,444/ under this head.

27. Thus the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
1.Loss of dependency Rs.23,52,060/
2.Loss of estate 15,000/
3.Towards spousal consortium (for 40,000/ petitioner No.1)

7
4.Towards filial consortium (for 80,000/ petitioners No.2 and 3)
5.Transportation of dead body and 15,000/ funeral expenses 6.Medical expenses 34,444/
Regarding liability:
The respondent No.2 have not admitted issuance of policy to the offending Auto.
Hence the petitioners to prove their case have got marked the copy of Policy as per Ex.P.15 during the cross examination of Rw.1 by way of confrontation.

Eventhough the RW.1 has denied it,
but they have not produced any supportive documents to show that the Ex.P.15 was not issued by them.
So as per Ex.,P.15 (SCCH3) 19 M.V.C.No.895/2020 the said policy was in force as on the date of accident.

Hence under these circumstances when the petitioners have proved the accident caused by the offending auto driver and the death of son of petitioner No.2 due to fatal injuries, then they are entitled for the compensation.
The said auto is owned by the respondent No.1 and insured with the respondent No.2 which is valid as on the date of accident.
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

29. With regard to apportionment is concerned, petitioner No.1 being the wife is entitled for 70%
and petitioners No.2 and 3 being the parents of the deceased are entitled for 15% each of the amount awarded.
Hence, the issue No.4 is answered in partly affirmative.
30. Issue No.5:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 3 as above and with regard to awarding the interest is concerned, the petitioners are entitled for simple interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit.
As such I proceed to pass the following: (SCCH3) 20 M.V.C.No.895/2020 ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec 166 of the M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part, with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for Rs.25,36,504/ (Twenty five lakhs thirty six thousand five hundred and four only) as compensation with interest at 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners.

However, in view of valid insurance policy, respondent No.2  Insurance Company is directed to pay the awarded compensation amount and shall deposit the same within time stipulated under section 168(3) of M.V. Act.
On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, petitioner No.1 is entitled for 70% of compensation and the petitioners No.2 and 3 are entitled for 15% each of compensation as awarded.

Out of the share amount of petitioner No.1 along with interest accrued, 40% of the amount shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized or schedule (SCCH3) 21 M.V.C.No.895/2020 bank for a period of three years and the remaining 60% of the amount shall be released to her through E payment on proper identification without any further proceedings.
However, PW.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.

Draw award accordingly.
